APA.one_line: Permian + Egypt + Suriname (Sailfish) E&P; low leverage but flat-to-negative forward EPS growth already largely priced by an 84% 12-month rally.
APA.reason: Cheap headline P/E and low leverage, but forward EPS growth is negative and the stock already re-rated hard on Suriname optionality; street upside is thin (7.5%). Not a clear mispricing either way.

COP.one_line: Best-in-class diversified low-cost E&P post-Marathon Oil merger; high quality but model flags valuation as demanding.
COP.reason: Premier balance sheet and multi-basin scale (quality), but the model's 'demanding' tag and modest FCF yield relative to price mean the market is already paying up for the merger synergies. Not a bargain today.

DVN.one_line: Permian-focused E&P grown via Grayson Mill acquisition; solid but unremarkable on every axis.
DVN.reason: Decent growth and high street upside (28%), but FCF yield is thin (1.5%) for a supposedly cheap E&P, suggesting heavy reinvestment. Fair, not exceptional; doesn't clear the quality-or-growth ≥4 bar.

EQT.one_line: Largest Appalachian gas producer with integrated midstream, positioned as a core LNG/data-center-power feedgas supplier.
EQT.reason: Negative near-term forward EPS/revenue growth is a comp/gas-price lap, not volume decline; FCF yield (7.7%) is healthy and leverage low (0.8x). Structural LNG-export and power-demand tailwind plus 33% street upside justify full diligence on the earnings trajectory.
sources: general knowledge of Appalachian gas/LNG feedgas dynamics

EXE.one_line: Largest US natural gas producer (Marcellus/Haynesville) formed via merger, geared to Gulf Coast LNG feedgas demand.
EXE.reason: Negative trailing growth reflects lapping high 2025 gas-price comps, not decline; low leverage (0.5x), 7.1% FCF yield, and the largest street upside in the batch (44.5%) merit full diligence, with integration/hedging risk flagged for review.

FANG.one_line: Premier low-cost Permian operator (post-Endeavor merger); one of the best-run pure-play E&Ps.
FANG.reason: Trailing P/E is depressed-base noise (43.4 vs NTM 9.7); normalized FCF yield (9.6%) implies the market is pricing near-zero growth against a genuinely low-cost, scaled Permian asset base. 25.6% street upside supports advancing.

red_flags: Historically elevated leverage (now improved to 0.8x); DAC/1PointFive is a cash-consuming, unproven business line
OXY.one_line: Diversified Permian E&P + OxyChem + carbon capture, with Berkshire Hathaway as a large anchor shareholder.
OXY.reason: Post-CrownRock integration is driving strong revenue/EPS growth and margins are best-in-class (30%); balance sheet has de-levered. Direct air capture optionality is a swing factor worth diligence, but core E&P/chemicals quality and growth clear the bar.

red_flags: Priced for perpetual growth: near-zero/negative FCF yield despite a 33.9x NTM P/E; thin analyst coverage (2 analysts) limits consensus reliability
TPL.one_line: Unique royalty + water-rights toll-taker on Permian land; exceptional margins and ROE but valuation has run far ahead of any plausible growth path.
TPL.reason: Best business model in the batch (60% margins, 37% ROE, net cash) but the price already assumes decades of above-trend royalty growth; near-zero FCF yield means required growth exceeds anything historically demonstrated. Great business, wrong price today.

PSX.one_line: Integrated refiner + midstream + chemicals (CPChem); cyclical refining margins now fully in the price after an 87% rally.
PSX.reason: Model already flags 'excessive' and street upside is negative (-1.5%), meaning consensus targets sit below the current price after the rally. Refining is a thin-margin, cyclical business without a durable moat premium here.

VLO.one_line: Best-in-class pure-play refiner; strong operator but the stock has more than doubled (+115% 12-month) into a cyclical refining upswing.
VLO.reason: Negative street upside (-6.9%) after the rally signals the current refining-margin environment is already fully reflected. Cyclical commodity business without enough margin of safety left at this price.

KMI.one_line: Dominant US natural gas pipeline network with LNG/power-demand growth narrative, but forward EPS growth is flat.
KMI.reason: Irreplaceable pipeline moat (quality), but 19.8x NTM P/E for essentially flat forward EPS growth and thin FCF yield (1.6%) against 4.2x leverage doesn't leave a margin of safety; the AI-power-demand growth story hasn't yet shown up in the numbers.

red_flags: High leverage (4.3x); integration risk from recent large acquisitions (EnLink, Medallion)
OKE.one_line: Diversified NGL/midstream operator grown rapidly via M&A; scale is improving but organic growth and FCF yield are modest.
OKE.reason: Low FCF yield (1.6%) and high leverage against a rich 14.7x NTM P/E leave little cushion; growth has been acquisition-driven rather than clearly organic, adding integration risk.

red_flags: High leverage (3.5x); heavy growth capex leaves ~0% FCF yield
TRGP.one_line: Premier Permian NGL gathering/processing franchise with extraordinary ROE (71%), but the stock is up 79% and priced for continued high growth.
TRGP.reason: Genuinely excellent midstream franchise, but PEG-like math (23.3x NTM P/E vs 15.6% forward growth) after a huge rally and negligible FCF yield mean the growth is now the consensus expectation, not a surprise.

red_flags: Negative FCF yield; high leverage (4.3x); worst-ranked name in the batch per the statistical model
WMB.one_line: Irreplaceable Transco gas pipeline franchise, but trading at 27x NTM earnings for essentially flat forward growth.
WMB.reason: Excellent asset (quality 4) but the valuation has decoupled from near-term growth entirely; negative FCF yield and high leverage compound the risk that this is priced for a demand ramp that hasn't materialized yet.

AMP.one_line: Capital-light wealth management + asset management franchise with a remarkable 63% ROE, trading at under 10x NTM earnings.
AMP.reason: Rare combination: strong moat (advisor network, capital-light model), 25% forward EPS growth, and a cheap absolute multiple (PEG ~0.4). Model already tags it 'fair'; the case for full diligence is straightforward.

red_flags: Industry-wide private-credit liquidity/redemption concerns and rising borrower stress flagged in press coverage (Mar 2026); Athene annuity book adds insurance-liability duration risk
APO.one_line: Alternative asset manager + Athene retirement/annuities platform; among the largest private-credit originators.
APO.reason: Cheap-looking 11.9x NTM P/E and strong growth, but trailing P/E of 43x signals real earnings volatility, and a March 2026 Zacks piece flagged mounting private-credit liquidity/redemption concerns across the sector that specifically named Apollo. Worth full diligence to size the risk rather than reject outright given no confirmed company-specific failure.

red_flags: Unusually high leverage metric (9.1x); negative 12-month momentum (-7.7%) amid sector-wide private-credit jitters
ARES.one_line: Private-credit-focused alternative asset manager; growing AUM but trailing multiple (55.7x) is rich and momentum has turned negative.
ARES.reason: Elevated leverage and a stock that's already declining suggest the market is pricing in some private-credit-cycle concern; without stronger evidence of mispricing, this doesn't clear the price_vs_growth bar today.

BLK.one_line: Dominant #1 global asset manager (iShares ETFs, Aladdin, expanding private-markets via GIP/HPS/Preqin deals).
BLK.reason: Best-in-class moat and platform breadth; 54% forward EPS growth (aided by recent acquisitions) against a 17.5x NTM multiple and 22% street upside is an attractive combination worth full diligence on how much growth is acquisition vs. organic.

red_flags: Prior BREIT redemption-queue episode (2022-2023) shows real-estate-fund liquidity mismatch risk can resurface
BX.one_line: Largest alternative asset manager globally, spanning PE, credit, real estate and infrastructure.
BX.reason: Best-in-class scale and fee-earning AUM growth (67% forward EPS growth) at a reasonable 16.7x NTM multiple; negative 12-month momentum (-12.8%) despite strong fundamentals looks like a possible entry point worth full diligence, with the BREIT-style liquidity risk flagged for review.

red_flags: Multi-year structural net outflows from legacy active mutual funds (secular decline in core franchise)
BEN.one_line: Legacy active manager (Franklin Templeton) diversifying into alternatives, but core mutual-fund business faces persistent AUM outflows.
BEN.reason: Cheap-looking 10.4x NTM P/E and a big rally (+53%) don't offset the structural decline in the core active-management franchise; negative FCF yield (-17.8%) is also a concern. Classic value-trap profile.

BNY.one_line: Largest global custody bank; scale-driven moat in asset servicing, collateral management and Pershing platform.
BNY.reason: Strong quality franchise with high margins (29%) and improving ROE; after a 51% rally the remaining street upside is modest (11.5%) but the moat and growth trajectory still justify a closer look.

red_flags: Negative ROE (-0.9%); missing/incomplete forward-earnings data signals earnings troubles; structural AUM pressure in active management (though offset partly by QQQ/ETF franchise)
IVZ.one_line: Traditional asset manager with a valuable ETF franchise (QQQ) but weak core profitability and negative ROE.
IVZ.reason: Model tags it 'excessive' despite a low headline P/E; negative ROE and incomplete growth data are disqualifying-quality red flags rather than a bargain. Same secular-decline pattern as Franklin Resources.

red_flags: Global Atlantic insurance affiliate adds earnings volatility and private-credit/annuity duration risk, consistent with sector-wide concerns flagged for peer Apollo in Mar 2026 press; worst statistical-model rank in the batch (495/500) and negative 12-month momentum (-15%)
KKR.one_line: Diversified alternative asset manager (PE, credit, infrastructure) plus Global Atlantic insurance/annuity platform.
KKR.reason: Cheap 13.6x NTM P/E and strong forward growth, but the worst model rank in the batch plus negative momentum warrant investigating whether the market is correctly pricing insurance-book/private-credit risk rather than dismissing the concern. Advancing for full diligence, not because it's a clean bargain.
sources: general knowledge; industry private-credit context from APO search

NTRS.one_line: Institutional/HNW custody and wealth-management franchise; solid quality but modest growth already priced in.
NTRS.reason: After a 40% rally, street upside has shrunk to just 4.9%, and forward EPS growth (8.9%) is unremarkable versus peers like STT and BNY. Good business, fully valued.

STT.one_line: Major global custodian and asset servicer (State Street/SSGA); strong recent growth acceleration.
STT.reason: 35% forward EPS growth against a 12.2x NTM multiple (PEG well under 1) even after a 69% rally is an attractive setup; still only 10% modeled upside so not a screaming bargain, but the quality/growth combination merits full diligence.

AXP.one_line: Premium closed-loop card network with an affluent, loyal customer base and best-in-class returns (34% ROE).
AXP.reason: Exceptional moat and consistently strong execution; 22% forward EPS growth at a 15.8x NTM multiple with 22.5% street upside is fairly priced for a top-tier franchise, not a bargain but not expensive either.

red_flags: Discover integration execution risk; near-prime consumer-credit exposure in a slowing labor market; the data card's reported revenue-growth figure (11.11) appears to be a data anomaly and should be re-verified
COF.one_line: Now owns its own card network after the Discover acquisition; cheap valuation but integration and credit-cycle risk warrant scrutiny.
COF.reason: 8.8x NTM P/E, a strong statistical-model rank (38), and 29% street upside stand out, but the model's own 'excessive' tag and near-prime credit exposure mean full diligence should focus on charge-off trends and integration progress before concluding this is simply cheap.

BAC.one_line: Second-largest US diversified bank with a dominant low-cost retail deposit franchise.
BAC.reason: Excellent statistical-model rank (19/500), 11.1x NTM P/E against 22% forward EPS growth (PEG ~0.5), and 21% street upside make this one of the more attractive names in the batch despite the model's own 'excessive' tag, which appears to reflect a narrower factor than headline valuation.

red_flags: Historically sub-par ROE (8.5%, still below peers) reflecting an unfinished multi-year restructuring
C.one_line: Multi-year restructuring story under CEO Jane Fraser (simplification, Banamex divestiture, cost cuts) with improving but still-low ROE.
C.reason: 39% forward EPS growth and a cheap 10.8x NTM P/E reflect real turnaround progress (32% momentum), but the weak statistical-model rank (418/500) signals the market still questions durability of the ROE improvement — exactly the kind of name that needs a real diligence pass rather than a quick reject or accept.

JPM.one_line: The gold-standard diversified bank (Dimon-led), with the best margins and returns in the group.
JPM.reason: Growth is modest (7% forward EPS) and street upside thin (9%), but best-in-class quality (35% margin, 18% ROE) justifies the premium; fair value for the top franchise, not a bargain, still worth confirming durability of trading/IB revenue.

PNC.one_line: Well-run super-regional bank with a diversified fee/lending mix and completed acquisition integration (BBVA USA).
PNC.reason: 18% forward EPS growth at a 10.8x NTM P/E (PEG ~0.6) with 22.6% street upside is an attractive combination for a solid quality-4 regional franchise; worth full diligence on credit quality trends.
